svg.text: 1 · The assembly pipeline is not a staircase — it is four loops chained by gates
Phases 0–10 with the software at each step. The back-edges are the point: most of the final quality comes from re-entering a phase, not from advancing to the next one.
cheap, fast, and the phase most often skipped — a wrong ploidy here silently poisons every later number
ploidy ≠ 2 → re-run the size model with the value you measured, not the one you assumed
The same failure caught at P8
the span / N50 gate is a two-sided test — too large means retained haplotigs, too small means over-purging or collapsed repeats
span ≫ estimate, or BUSCO D high → re-purge, tune --hom-cov
it collapses heterozygous sites. That is
every join added here is inference, not observation — the one loop that genuinely needs a human eye on the contact map
misjoins or bowtie patterns in the contact map → curate again
Forcing scaffolds to hit a predetermined
four orthogonal axes, four different tools — no single number certifies an assembly
high D → back to Loop 2 · fragmented → back to Loop 3 · this is the expensive failure

Resolution does not improve monotonically along this path. Loops 1–3 buy contiguity by spending certainty; Loop 4 is the only place certainty is measured. A pipeline drawn without back-edges is a pipeline nobody has run.
